title: Per-token velocity calibration suite for core models
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Build and maintain a focused microbenchmarking suite that characterizes per-token emission rates (tokens/sec) and p95 latency across our core model set under realistic request patterns. This ticket covers instrumentation, workload synthesis, stable baselining, alerting for regressions, and CI integration so model or runtime changes cannot regress tokens/sec or tail latency silently. The suite must be robust to KV-cache warmup variation and should include synthetic and replay-based workload modes. Output must include short, shareable artifacts for releases and on-call runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible harness (CLI + containerized runner) that produces steady-state tokens/sec and p95 reports for each core model within < 5 minutes of run time
Per-model baseline artifacts stored in the performance artifact bucket and exposed in the Grafana dashboard with historical medians and p95 bands
Regression detector that raises a CI failure or paged alert when a model/runtime change causes >10% drop in median tokens/sec or >20% increase in p95 compared to baseline over three consecutive runs
KV-cache aware mode: benchmark can run cold, warm, and warmed-with-prefix (to mimic chat reuse) and annotate results accordingly
Canary job in GitHub Actions that runs lightweight suite on PRs touching runtime, kernel selection, or scheduler layers
Runbook entry added to the on-call playbook describing triage steps and rollback thresholds
tasks: Instrument runner to capture per-token throughput and p95 histograms (include tags for model, seq_len, batch_size, kv_state)
Implement synthetic workload generator with configurable token emission profile and burst patterns
Add replay harness to use production traces (anonymized) for more realistic pacing
Create Grafana dashboard panels with medians, p95 series and anomaly bands
Write regression detector service (stateless binary) that compares latest run to baseline and returns non-zero exit code for CI
Add GitHub Action workflow and a lightweight nightly job for full baseline refresh
Author runbook and a short Confluence design doc describing methodology
